section_1.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1:00)
section_1.content: Brief review of 2D linear transformations (matrix-vector multiplication) and the basis vectors i, j, k. Introduce 3D space as a grid of vectors where any point is defined by its coordinates (x, y, z).
section_1.example: Visualizing a 3D unit cube composed of vectors i(1,0,0), j(0,1,0), and k(0,0,1) anchored at the origin.

section_2.title: The Matrix Representation (1:00)
section_2.content: Explain that a 3D transformation is defined by where the basis vectors land. A 3x3 matrix tracks the new positions of i, j, and k. The columns of the matrix represent these transformed basis vectors.
section_2.example: A 'Robot Arm' character: The matrix columns describe how the arm's base (i), mid-section (j), and gripper (k) are oriented in 3D space after rotation.

section_3.title: Visualizing Transformations (1:30)
section_3.content: Demonstrate the three primary types of transformations: Scaling (stretching along axes), Rotation (rotating around an axis), and Shearing. Show how these change the 'grid' of the entire 3D space.
section_3.example: A 'Digital Character' model: Scaling it to make it taller, rotating it to face the camera, and shearing to create a 'speed effect' or slant.

section_4.title: Determinants & Invertibility (1:00)
section_4.content: Define the determinant as the 'volume scaling factor.' Explain that if the determinant is zero, the 3D space collapses into a 2D plane or 1D line, losing information.
section_4.example: A 'Space-Folding Device': If the determinant is zero, a 3D object inside the device is flattened into a 'paper-thin' 2D shape, illustrating loss of dimensionality.

section_5.title: Summary & Application (0:30)
section_5.content: Recap: Linear transformations are matrix-vector products. They are the engine behind 3D computer graphics, game engine physics, and robotics movement.
section_5.example: The final assembly of a 3D character game engine: Matrix multiplication transforms the character from local model space into the global game world.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=20, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Map to right side of screen: x from 1 to 6, y from 2.5 down to -2.5
